newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge sentences Ferber to 33 months in prison.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge sentences Ferber to 33 months in prison.

text.p: A Federal judge here on Thursday said he sentenced municipal banker Mark Ferber, a former partner with Lazard Freres & Co, to 33 months in prison, two years' probation and a $1 million fine.
Ferber was convicted in August on 58 of 61 fraud and corruption charges involving a contract he maintained with Merrill Lynch & Co to advise government clients on the municipal bond market.
On Wednesday U.S. Federal Judge William Young during a sentence hearing dropped 11 of the 58 counts.
The allegations and charges centered on whether or not a contract between Ferber and Merrill Lynch was adequately disclosed to Ferber's government clients in the municipal bond market.

Merrill Lynch and Lazard Freres settled with the U.S. Attorneys Office late last year over the matter, paying a total of $24 million in fines. Neither firm admitted or denied guilt in connection with the settlement.

Judge Young said in pronouncing the sentence that he was adjusting it downward from a proposed 37 to 46-month sentence that he had been mulling yesterday because of the disparity in treatment Ferber had received compared with the fines Merrill Lynch and Lazard Freres were allowed to pay in the matter. ((--U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650))
